title: Prakrama 1, Sarga 6. The Description of the Pastimes from Birth among the Childhood Plays
html:
Vishvambhara's infancy: the naming, His form, childhood plays; the wandering brahmana; the broken pots; the teaching on pure and impure; the brick thrown at His mother; the two coconuts; the sound of ankle bells

Verse 1

ततः कालेन कियता जानुचंक्रमणं शिशोः।
दृष्ट्वा प्रहर्षमाप्तौ तौ दम्पती कलभाषिणः॥१॥

tataḥ kālena kiyatā jānucaṁkramaṇaṁ śiśoḥ|
dṛṣṭvā praharṣamāptau tau dampatī kalabhāṣiṇaḥ||1||

tatah — then; kalena — after a time; kiyata — some; janu-chankramanam — the crawling on knees; shishoh — of the infant; drishtva — seeing; praharsham — great joy; aptau — obtained; tau — the two; dampati — husband and wife; kala-bhashinah — sweetly babbling.

1Some time passed, and the husband and wife, watching their sweetly babbling infant crawl about on His knees, were filled with great joy.

Verse 2

शोणपद्माभवदने द्विजराजस्य रश्मयः।
सुस्मिते भान्ति साधूनां मनोध्वान्तापहारिणः॥२॥

śoṇapadmābhavadane dvijarājasya raśmayaḥ|
susmite bhānti sādhūnāṁ manodhvāntāpahāriṇaḥ||2||

shona-padma-abha-vadane — on the face like a red lotus; dvija-rajasya — of the king of the twice-born (the moon; also — of the teeth); rashmayah — the rays; su-smite — smiling; bhanti — shine; sadhunam — of the saints; manah-dhvanta-apaharinah — dispelling the darkness of the mind.

2On His smiling face, like a red lotus, shone the rays of "the king of the twice-born"1, dispelling the darkness in the minds of the saints.

Verse 3

पुरा बिभर्त्यसौ विश्वमिति चक्रे पिता स्वयम्।
श्रीमद्विश्वम्भर इति नाम तस्य सुशोभनम्॥३॥

purā bibhartyasau viśvamiti cakre pitā svayam|
śrīmadviśvambhara iti nāma tasya suśobhanam||3||

pura — of old (and ever); bibharti — sustains; asau — he; vishvam — the universe; iti — thus (thinking); chakre — gave; pita — the father; svayam — himself; shrimad-vishvambharah — Sriman Vishvambhara; iti — thus; nama — the name; tasya — to him; su-shobhanam — most beautiful.

3"He has sustained the universe from of old," thought the father, and he himself gave Him the most beautiful name Sriman Vishvambhara2.

Verse 4

तप्तकाञ्चनगौराङ्गो लसत्पद्मायतेक्षणः।
प्रभञ्जनाम्बरो रौप्यहारी मालालको हरिः॥४॥

taptakāñcanagaurāṅgo lasatpadmāyatekṣaṇaḥ|
prabhañjanāmbaro raupyahārī mālālako hariḥ||4||

tapta-kanchana-gaura-angah — with a body golden like molten gold; lasat-padma-ayata-ikshanah — with eyes wide like shining lotuses; prabhanjana-ambarah — clad in the wind (naked); raupya-hari — wearing a silver necklace; mala-alakah — with a garland in his curls; harih — Hari.

4Hari's body gleamed like molten gold, His eyes were wide as shining lotuses; clad only in the wind, He wore a silver necklace and a garland in His curls.

Verse 5

राकासुधाकरमुखः कलवागमृतान्वितः।
मधुराकृतिरामुक्तकङ्कणाङ्गदभूषणः॥५॥

rākāsudhākaramukhaḥ kalavāgamṛtānvitaḥ|
madhurākṛtirāmuktakaṅkaṇāṅgadabhūṣaṇaḥ||5||

raka-sudhakara-mukhah — with a face like the full moon; kala-vag-amrita-anvitah — endowed with the nectar of sweet babble; madhura-akritih — charming in form; amukta-kankana-angada-bhushanah — adorned with bracelets and armlets put on him.

5His face was like the full moon, His babble sweet as nectar; bracelets on His wrists and armlets on His arms adorned the charming child.

Verse 6

भङ्गहिङ्गुलरक्ताब्जकरपादतलः शुचिः।
ववृधे कलया नित्यं शुक्लपक्ष इव द्युराट्॥६॥

bhaṅgahiṅgularaktābjakarapādatalaḥ śuciḥ|
vavṛdhe kalayā nityaṁ śuklapakṣa iva dyurāṭ||6||

bhanga-hingula-rakta-abja-kara-pada-talah — with palms and soles red as a lotus or ground vermilion; shuchih — pure; vavridhe — grew; kalaya — digit by digit; nityam — constantly; shukla-pakshe — in the bright fortnight; iva — like; dyurat — the king of the sky (the moon).

6Pure, His palms and soles red as a lotus or ground vermilion, He grew day by day, waxing digit by digit like the moon in the bright fortnight.

Verse 7

ततः कालेन शोणाभ्यां पादाभ्याममितद्युतिः।
अटन्विरहजं तापं मेदिन्याः संजहार सः॥७॥

tataḥ kālena śoṇābhyāṁ pādābhyāmamitadyutiḥ|
aṭanvirahajaṁ tāpaṁ medinyāḥ saṁjahāra saḥ||7||

tatah — then; kalena — in time; shonabhyam — with red; padabhyam — feet; amita-dyutih — of boundless radiance; atan — walking; viraha-jam — born of separation; tapam — the burning; medinyah — of the earth; samjahara — removed; sah — he.

7In time the infant of boundless radiance began to walk, and treading with His red feet He soothed the earth's burning, born of separation (from Him)3.

Verse 8

तीर्थभ्रमणशीलस्य द्विजस्यान्नं जनार्दनः।
भुक्त्वा तं स्मारयामास नन्दगेहकुतूहलम्॥८॥

tīrthabhramaṇaśīlasya dvijasyānnaṁ janārdanaḥ|
bhuktvā taṁ smārayāmāsa nandagehakutūhalam||8||

tirtha-bhramana-shilasya — given to wandering among holy places; dvijasya — of the brahmana; annam — the food; janardanah — Janardana; bhuktva — having eaten; tam — him; smarayamasa — reminded of; nanda-geha-kutuhalam — the wonder in the house of Nanda.

8Janardana ate the food of a brahmana who wandered among the holy places, and so reminded him of the wonder in the house of Nanda4.

Verse 9

वयस्यैर्बालकैः सार्धं विहरंस्तरुपल्लवैः।
आहताः शिशवः सर्वे विचक्रुः पुरतो मुदा॥९॥

vayasyairbālakaiḥ sārdhaṁ viharaṁstarupallavaiḥ|
āhatāḥ śiśavaḥ sarve vicakruḥ purato mudā||9||

vayasyaih — with companions; balakaih — boys; sardham — together; viharan — playing; taru-pallavaih — with shoots of trees; ahatah — struck (with them); shishavah — the children; sarve — all; vichakruh — romped; puratah — before (him); muda — joyfully.

9He played with the boys of His age, (swinging) shoots of trees, and the children, struck by them, all romped joyfully before Him.

Verse 10

भुवि तिष्ठन्पदैकेन जानुनान्यस्य जानुकम्।
पस्पर्श मर्कटीं लीलां कुर्वन्मायार्भको हरिः॥१०॥

bhuvi tiṣṭhanpadaikena jānunānyasya jānukam|
pasparśa markaṭīṁ līlāṁ kurvanmāyārbhako hariḥ||10||

bhuvi — on the ground; tishthan — standing; pada-ekena — on one foot; januna — with the knee; anyasya — of the other; janukam — the knee; pasparsha — touched; markatim — monkey; lilam — play; kurvan — performing; maya-arbhakah — a child by his maya (appearing as a child); harih — Hari.

10Hari, appearing as a child by His yogamaya5, played like a monkey: standing on one foot, He would touch another boy's knee with His knee.

Verse 11

एकदा धर्तुमात्मानमुद्यतां जननीं रुषा।
वीक्ष्य कोपपरिपूर्णो भाजनानि बभञ्ज सः॥११॥

ekadā dhartumātmānamudyatāṁ jananīṁ ruṣā|
vīkṣya kopaparipūrṇo bhājanāni babhañja saḥ||11||

ekada — once; dhartum — to seize; atmanam — him; udyatam — ready; jananim — the mother; rusha — in anger; vikshya — seeing; kopa-paripurnah — full of anger; bhajanani — the pots; babhanja — broke; sah — he.

11Once, seeing His mother angrily about to seize Him, He grew angry Himself and smashed the pots.

Verse 12

पुरा भग्ने च भाण्डे यं यशोदा पशुरज्जुभिः।
बबन्ध वेपिता तस्य भयाद्वीक्ष्य मुखं शची॥१२॥

purā bhagne ca bhāṇḍe yaṁ yaśodā paśurajjubhiḥ|
babandha vepitā tasya bhayādvīkṣya mukhaṁ śacī||12||

pura — once; bhagne — when was broken; cha — and; bhande — the pot; yam — whom; yashoda — Yashoda; pashu-rajjubhih — with cattle ropes; babandha — bound; vepita — trembling; tasya — his; bhayat — from fear; vikshya — looking at; mukham — the face; shachi — Shachi.

12He whom Yashoda once bound with cattle ropes for a broken pot6 — Him Shachi now feared: looking at His face, she trembled.

Verse 13

उपर्युपरि विन्यस्तत्यक्तमृद्भाण्डसंहतौ।
उपविश्याशुचौ देशे मातुरग्रे जहास सः॥१३॥

uparyupari vinyastatyaktamṛdbhāṇḍasaṁhatau|
upaviśyāśucau deśe māturagre jahāsa saḥ||13||

upari-upari — one upon another; vinyasta-tyakta-mrid-bhanda-samhatau — on a heap of discarded clay pots piled; upavishya — sitting down; ashuchau — impure; deshe — in a place; matuh — of the mother; agre — in front; jahasa — laughed; sah — he.

13Then He sat down in an impure place, on a heap of discarded clay pots piled one upon another, and laughed in front of His mother.

Verse 14

तं दृष्ट्वा सा शची प्राह त्यज तात जुगुप्सितम्।
स्थानं शुद्धं पुनः स्नात्वा ममाङ्कारोहणं कुरु॥१४॥

taṁ dṛṣṭvā sā śacī prāha tyaja tāta jugupsitam|
sthānaṁ śuddhaṁ punaḥ snātvā mamāṅkārohaṇaṁ kuru||14||

tam — him; drishtva — seeing; sa — she; shachi — Shachi; praha — said; tyaja — leave; tata — child; jugupsitam — the loathsome; sthanam — place; shuddham — cleanly; punah — again; snatva — having bathed; mama — my; anka-arohanam — climbing onto the lap; kuru — do.

14Seeing this, Shachi said: "Child, come away from that loathsome place! Bathe again, be clean, and climb onto my lap."

Verse 15

एवमुक्ते तु तां प्राह भगवान्सर्वतत्त्ववित्।
दत्तात्रेयस्य भावैकपूर्णः सर्वज्ञपूरकः॥१५॥

evamukte tu tāṁ prāha bhagavānsarvatattvavit|
dattātreyasya bhāvaikapūrṇaḥ sarvajñapūrakaḥ||15||

evam — thus; ukte — when was spoken; tu — and; tam — to her; praha — said; bhagavan — Bhagavan; sarva-tattva-vit — knower of all truths; dattatreyasya — of Dattatreya; bhava-eka-purnah — wholly filled with the mood; sarva-jna-purakah — completing (the knowledge) of the all-knowing.

15At these words Bhagavan, the knower of all truths, wholly imbued with the mood of Dattatreya7, who completes (the knowledge) of the all-knowing, answered her:

Verse 16

शृणु शुचिरशुचिर्वा कल्पनामात्रमेतत्क्षितिजलपवनाग्निव्योमचित्तं जगद्धि।
विततविभवपूर्वाद्वैतपादाब्ज एको हरिरिह करुणाब्धिर्भाति नान्यत्प्रतीहि॥१६॥

śṛṇu śuciraśucirvā kalpanāmātrametatkṣitijalapavanāgnivyomacittaṁ jagaddhi|
vitatavibhavapūrvādvaitapādābja eko haririha karuṇābdhirbhāti nānyatpratīhi||16||

shrinu — listen; shuchih — pure; ashuchih — impure; va — or; kalpana-matram — a mere notion; etat — this; kshiti-jala-pavana-agni-vyoma-chittam — (made of) earth, water, air, fire, ether and mind; jagat — the world; hi — for; vitata-vibhava-purva-advaita-pada-abjah — whose lotus feet are non-dual and prior to all the spread-out manifestation; ekah — the one; harih — Hari; iha — here; karuna-abdhih — the ocean of compassion; bhati — shines; na — not; anyat — anything else; pratihi — know.

16"Listen: pure and impure are mere notions of the mind. For the world is (only) earth, water, air, fire, ether and mind; and here shines only the one Hari, the ocean of compassion, whose lotus feet are non-dual and prior to all the outspread manifestation. Know that there is nothing else8.

Verse 17

अतः पवित्र एवास्मि नापवित्रः कथंचन।
जानीहि मातर्नान्यां त्वं शङ्कां कर्तुमिहार्हसि॥१७॥

ataḥ pavitra evāsmi nāpavitraḥ kathaṁcana|
jānīhi mātarnānyāṁ tvaṁ śaṅkāṁ kartumihārhasi||17||

atah — therefore; pavitrah — pure; eva — indeed; asmi — I am; na — not; apavitrah — impure; kathamchana — in any way; janihi — know; matah — O mother; na — not; anyam — other; tvam — you; shankam — doubt; kartum — to have; iha — here; arhasi — should.

17Therefore I am pure and in no way impure. Know this, mother, and harbour no other doubt here."

Verse 18

एवमुक्ते सुते सा तं करे संगृह्य सत्वरा।
आनीय स्नापयामास स्वर्णदीस्वच्छवारिभिः॥१८॥

evamukte sute sā taṁ kare saṁgṛhya satvarā|
ānīya snāpayāmāsa svarṇadīsvacchavāribhiḥ||18||

evam — thus; ukte — when had spoken; sute — the son; sa — she; tam — him; kare — by the hand; samgrihya — taking; satvara — hastily; aniya — bringing; snapayamasa — bathed; svarnadi-svachchha-varibhih — with the clear waters of the heavenly river (Ganga).

18When her son had spoken thus, she hastily took Him by the hand, led Him (to the river) and bathed Him in the clear waters of the heavenly river.

Verse 19

अथ कतिपये काले मुक्तमृद्भाण्डसंहतौ।
उपविष्टं सुतं वीक्ष्य शची वाग्भिरताडयत्॥१९॥

atha katipaye kāle muktamṛdbhāṇḍasaṁhatau|
upaviṣṭaṁ sutaṁ vīkṣya śacī vāgbhiratāḍayat||19||

atha — then; katipaye — after some; kale — time; mukta-mrid-bhanda-samhatau — on a heap of thrown-away clay pots; upavishtam — seated; sutam — the son; vikshya — seeing; shachi — Shachi; vagbhih — with words; atadayat — scolded.

19After some time Shachi again saw her son seated on a heap of thrown-away clay pots and scolded Him:

Verse 20

अपवित्रे निषिद्धेऽपि स्थाने त्वं मन्दधीः कथम्।
तिष्ठसीति वचः श्रुत्वा मातुः क्रोधसमन्वितः॥२०॥

apavitre niṣiddhe'pi sthāne tvaṁ mandadhīḥ katham|
tiṣṭhasīti vacaḥ śrutvā mātuḥ krodhasamanvitaḥ||20||

apavitre — impure; nishiddhe — forbidden; api — even; sthane — in a place; tvam — you; manda-dhih — foolish one; katham — why; tishthasi — stay; iti — thus; vachah — the words; shrutva — hearing; matuh — of the mother; krodha-samanvitah — filled with anger.

20"Foolish one! Why do You sit in an impure, forbidden place?" Hearing these words of His mother, filled with anger,

Verse 21

श्रीमद्विश्वम्भरः प्राह मूढे नास्त्यशुचिः क्वचित्।
उक्तं मयैतत्पूर्वं ते तत्किं मां त्वं विगर्हसि॥२१॥

śrīmadviśvambharaḥ prāha mūḍhe nāstyaśuciḥ kvacit|
uktaṁ mayaitatpūrvaṁ te tatkiṁ māṁ tvaṁ vigarhasi||21||

shrimad-vishvambharah — Sriman Vishvambhara; praha — said; mudhe — foolish woman; na asti — there is not; ashuchih — impurity; kvachit — anywhere; uktam — told; maya — by me; etat — this; purvam — before; te — to you; tat — so; kim — why; mam — me; tvam — you; vigarhasi — reproach.

21Sriman Vishvambhara said: "Foolish woman! There is nothing impure anywhere. I told you this before — so why do you reproach Me?"

Verse 22

इत्युक्त्वा वदने तस्या इष्टकां प्राहिणोद्रुषा।
तदाघातेन व्यथिता मूर्च्छिता निपपात सा॥२२॥

ityuktvā vadane tasyā iṣṭakāṁ prāhiṇodruṣā|
tadāghātena vyathitā mūrcchitā nipapāta sā||22||

iti — thus; uktva — having spoken; vadane — at the face; tasyah — her; ishtakam — a brick; prahinot — threw; rusha — in anger; tat-aghatena — by that blow; vyathita — pained; murchchhita — fainting; nipapata — fell; sa — she.

22With these words He angrily threw a brick at her face. Stricken by the blow, she fainted and fell.

Verse 23

तदा सर्वाः समागत्य स्त्रियस्तां शीतलैर्जलैः।
सिषिचुः स्म तदा तत्र हरिर्मानुषकर्मकृत्॥२३॥

tadā sarvāḥ samāgatya striyastāṁ śītalairjalaiḥ|
siṣicuḥ sma tadā tatra harirmānuṣakarmakṛt||23||

tada — then; sarvah — all; samagatya — gathering; striyah — the women; tam — her; shitalaih — with cool; jalaih — water; sishichuh sma — sprinkled; tada — then; tatra — there; harih — Hari; manusha-karma-krit — acting in human ways.

23Then all the women gathered and sprinkled her with cool water. And then Hari, who acts in human ways, came there

Verse 24

आगत्य प्ररुरोदाशु मातर्मातरिति स्वयम्।
श्रीहस्तं तन्मुखे न्यस्य सर्वदुःखापहारकम्॥२४॥

āgatya prarurodāśu mātarmātariti svayam|
śrīhastaṁ tanmukhe nyasya sarvaduḥkhāpahārakam||24||

agatya — coming; praruroda — burst into tears; ashu — at once; matah matah — mother, mother; iti — thus; svayam — himself; shri-hastam — his beautiful hand; tat-mukhe — on her face; nyasya — placing; sarva-duhkha-apaharakam — which removes every sorrow.

24and at once burst into tears Himself: "Mother, mother!" — and laid on her face His beautiful hand, which takes away every sorrow.

Verse 25

ततः प्रबुद्धा सा सद्यः क्रोडे कृत्वा सुतं शची।
मुमोद वत्सलातीव पुत्रस्नेहातिविह्वला॥२५॥

tataḥ prabuddhā sā sadyaḥ kroḍe kṛtvā sutaṁ śacī|
mumoda vatsalātīva putrasnehātivihvalā||25||

tatah — then; prabuddha — come to her senses; sa — she; sadyah — at once; krode — on her lap; kritva — placing; sutam — the son; shachi — Shachi; mumoda — rejoiced; vatsala — loving; ativa — greatly; putra-sneha-ati-vihvala — overwhelmed with love for her son.

25Shachi came to herself at once, took her son onto her lap and, beside herself with love for Him, rejoiced with all her heart.

Verse 26

ततो जगद्गुरुं प्राह काचिद्धर्षपरायणा।
परिहासपरा मात्रे नारिकेलफलद्वयम्॥२६॥

tato jagadguruṁ prāha kāciddharṣaparāyaṇā|
parihāsaparā mātre nārikelaphaladvayam||26||

tatah — then; jagad-gurum — to the teacher of the world; praha — said; kachit — a certain (woman); harsha-parayana — merry; parihasa-para — fond of jest; matre — to the mother; narikela-phala-dvayam — two coconuts.

26Then a merry woman, fond of a joke, said to the Teacher of the world: "Go and fetch two coconuts for Your mother,

Verse 27

समानीय प्रयच्छास्यै तदा स्वस्था भविष्यति।
न चेन्मरिष्यति तदा किमुपायं करिष्यसि॥२७॥

samānīya prayacchāsyai tadā svasthā bhaviṣyati|
na cenmariṣyati tadā kimupāyaṁ kariṣyasi||27||

samaniya — bringing; prayachchha — give; asyai — to her; tada — then; svastha — well; bhavishyati — she will be; na chet — if not; marishyati — she will die; tada — then; kim — what; upayam — remedy; karishyasi — will you take.

27bring them and give them to her — then she will be well. If not, she will die — and what will You do then?"

Verse 28

Thus ends the sixth sarga, "The Description of the Pastimes from Birth among the Childhood Plays" (Balya-krida: janmadi-lila-varnana), of the first prakrama of the great poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. "The king of the twice-born" (dvijaraja) is the moon; but "the twice-born" (dvija) are also the teeth: a play on words — the shining of His teeth in His smile.
  2. Vishvambhara means "He who sustains the universe."
  3. The earth, according to tradition, suffered in separation from Krishna's feet after His departure.
  4. The story of the pilgrim brahmana whose food, offered to the Lord, was eaten by the infant Nimai; so too the infant Krishna once ate the food of a wandering brahmana in the house of Nanda.
  5. Yogamaya is the Lord's internal, spiritual energy, by which He Himself conceals or reveals Himself in His pastimes (cf. Bhagavad-gita 7.25: "I am not manifest to all, being veiled by yogamaya"). It is not the external maya that deludes living beings; the Lord is never subject to that.
  6. An allusion to the Bhagavata Purana (10.9): Yashoda bound the child Krishna when He broke the pot of curd.
  7. Dattatreya is an incarnation of the Lord, an avadhuta who made no distinction between pure and impure.
  8. The Lord speaks in the mood of the avadhuta Dattatreya (v. 15). "There is nothing else" means that nothing exists apart from Hari — the world is His energy (cf. Bhagavata Purana 1.5.20: the universe is the Lord Himself, and yet He is distinct from it). This is not a doctrine of impersonal oneness: the "non-dual" here is Hari Himself, a person, "the ocean of compassion," with His lotus feet.
  9. The end of the line is corrupt in the sources; the reading is tentative.
  10. The Vatsa clan (gotra) is the clan of Jagannatha Mishra (cf. "the Vatsya").
  11. The people Shachi saw in the house were evidently the gods, come to worship the Lord.
